coverage_note: Long English rule-discussion stretches (15:00-20:10, 36:00-48:35, 1:01:40-1:04:00). 55:30-1:01:10 Medi and part of Amal are Latin-transliterated. Rule quizzes (16:19-17:08 'does aghlab take el-', 28:15, 50:25-51:10) are questions/answers about the rule, not counted. No echo-candidates file for 2026-10-05. Pronunciation-only: بوع for بقع (07:10), بتي for بطيء (15:04), عبوي (27:41), ممرّة (02:45), أملكت (03:31). 56:32 ruhna / rawahna: Amal offered an alternative ('Or'), not a fix. 53:21 تاني إجازة self-fixed to اجتماع before her.

rows.amal_said: الصباح. either الصباح or في الصباح.
rows.why: He said bare صباح for 'this morning'; Amal recast الصباح and said either الصباح or في الصباح, he repeated في الصباح.
rows.english: I had an important client this morning.

rows.amal_said: جهزت is like prepared... بس عملت أو طبخت would be a better fit for food.
rows.why: For cooking a dish Amal said جهزت gives 'prepared everything' and عملت or طبخت is the right verb for food.
He said خريف (autumn) for lamb; Amal echoed it back questioningly and he changed to خروف (sheet: lamb | La7em 5aruf | لحم خروف).

rows.amal_said: واحدة. Because it's ساعة. ... الساعة واحدة or just واحدة.
rows.why: Clock time takes the feminine number; Amal gave واحدة and explained it is because of الساعة.

rows.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة، أو قميص رسمي
rows.why: Asked what he is wearing today he used the habitual بلبس; the participle لابس fits (B15 not taught yet, filed only).
rows.english: Today I'm wearing a formal white shirt.

rows.why: Stains are ON the shirt: Amal recast عليه بقع for his عنده (بوع for بقع is a dropped ق, S4, not counted).
rows.english: and it has stains on it

rows.why: Answering who put stains on it (past) he used present بحط; Amal recast حطيت and he said 'that's right. أنا حطيت'.

rows.medi_said: Do I know the word for beets? ... أنا نسيت الـ...
rows.why: He asked for beets and Amal supplied بنجر (sheet: beet | Banjar | بنجر).

rows.medi_said: wait for you would be ستنت لك، ستنيت لك،
rows.why: استنى takes a direct object ending, not لـ; Amal recast استنيتك and he said 'There's no il. Okay.'
He stacked two 'me' endings (لي + ني); Amal said 'No. Try again' and gave حكيت لي.

rows.amal_said: هلأ قصدك إنه أغلب ما بتحتاج ال...
rows.why: mish before a verb; Amal restated his answer with ما بتحتاج and he then said ما بتحتاج at 17:51.

rows.medi_said: so ٱغْلَب most people because it's not ٱلنَّاسُ, so it'd be ٱغْلَب النَّاسِ.
rows.amal_said: أغلب after it there's ال. Why did you take it out? ... Whatever the word is after most we say ال.
rows.why: Engine wrote ٱغْلَب النَّاسِ but Amal's 'Why did you take it out?' and his 'Because ناس is not definitive' show he said أغلب ناس without el-.
rows.proposed_rule: aghlab / nafs are followed by a noun WITH el- and never take el- themselves: aghlab el-naas, nafs el-ashkhaas (not el-nafs, not ashkhaas el-nafs)

rows.medi_said: How do you say my clothes? Is it أَوَا...
rows.why: He asked how to say 'my clothes' and Amal supplied it (sheet: clothes (plural) | Awaa3i | أواعي).

rows.amal_said: نفس never takes ال before it. Al-always after it.
rows.why: He put el- on نفس; Amal named the rule that نفس never takes ال before it, only the noun after it does.
rows.proposed_rule: aghlab / nafs are followed by a noun WITH el- and never take el- themselves: aghlab el-naas, nafs el-ashkhaas (not el-nafs, not ashkhaas el-nafs)

rows.why: For 'nothing (similar)' he said مش إشي; Amal recast ما في إشي and he repeated ما في إشي.
After the definite نفس الأشخاص the link is اللي not إنه (my reading); Amal had him rebuild it as إحنا بنكره نفس الأشخاص without naming this.
rows.english: the same people that we hate

rows.amal_said: صح. ... نفس never takes ال before it always after and it's before the noun.
rows.why: He put نفس after the noun with el-; Amal said it comes before the noun and never takes ال, he fixed to نفس الأشخاص.
rows.proposed_rule: aghlab / nafs are followed by a noun WITH el- and never take el- themselves: aghlab el-naas, nafs el-ashkhaas (not el-nafs, not ashkhaas el-nafs)

rows.amal_said: Why ال آخر؟ ... آخر الأسبوع صح، بس مش ال آخر الأسبوع. أغلب آخر الأسبوع.
rows.why: In a noun chain only the last noun takes el-; Amal said 'مش ال آخر الأسبوع' and named the idafa rule.
He flipped the idafa order; Amal recast أغلب آخر الأسبوع and he repeated it.
انبسط takes بـ/في; Amal said bil-shaati (engine wrote بلشات) and he said 'I forgot about انبسط... بالشاطئ'.

rows.amal_said: شو الأول؟ What's feminine of أول؟ ... بدلة.
rows.why: Engine wrote الأولى but Amal's echo شو الأول؟ shows he said الأول with feminine بدلة; he fixed to أولى.
He used أكثر (most) for 'best'; Amal prompted best/better and he said أحسن.

rows.amal_said: Ahsan. One. Now, what does one mean?
rows.why: For 'the best one' about an outfit he said إشي; Amal prompted 'One' and he built أحسن واحدة.
rows.proposed_rule: 'the best one / the first one' needs waahed / waahde after the ordinal or superlative: a7san waahde, awwal waahed

rows.amal_said: Laish kundaret? ... It's not idafa here, it's just adjective. ... You're missing an L.
rows.why: Noun + definite adjective needs el- on both; Amal asked why kundaret (idafa -t) and said 'You're missing an L', he fixed to الكندارة الأخيرة.
'The beginning of my day' needs the possessive يومي; Amal prompted and he said أول يومي.
He dropped 'my'; Amal repeated 'My whole day' and he said كل يومي.
For 'boring' he reused يزعل (saddening); Amal gave بيزهق (sheet: boring / causes boredom | beyzahheq | بيزهق).
rows.english: The end of the lesson was boring.

rows.why: العربية is the feminine / the language; for 'Arabs' Amal gave the plural العرب or العربيين.
Right after her أغلب العربيين he dropped el- after أغلب and she let it pass (engine may have lost the el-).
rows.proposed_rule: aghlab / nafs are followed by a noun WITH el- and never take el- themselves: aghlab el-naas, nafs el-ashkhaas (not el-nafs, not ashkhaas el-nafs)

rows.amal_said: No، go on. أول شو؟ ... What's one?
rows.why: 'the same as the first one' left out واحد; Amal asked أول شو / What's one? and he said أول واحد.
rows.english: the same as the first one
rows.proposed_rule: 'the best one / the first one' needs waahed / waahde after the ordinal or superlative: a7san waahde, awwal waahed

rows.why: He said abel ma (before) for 'after'; Amal said 'After' and he changed to ba'id ma.
Past ending for 'we' is -na; Amal stressed 'we saw' and he fixed to shufna.

rows.medi_said: Ba'id ma shufna. After we saw...
rows.amal_said: That. You didn't-- You did-- You need a that here.
rows.why: Amal said he needs 'that' after 'we saw' and he added Enna (enno).
rows.proposed_rule: A clause after a seeing / knowing verb is introduced by enno (that): ba3ed ma shufna enno...

rows.why: Past 'was' needs kaan; Amal said 'Was, was' and he added kan nafs il-ishi.
rows.english: the second restaurant was the same

rows.why: He used singular 'your friend' for 'your friends'; Amal said 'Friends' and he switched to the plural sahabik.
A definite (possessed) noun takes an el- adjective that agrees in plural; Amal said no and gave sahabak al-thaniyin.

rows.amal_said: What is difference? They are different. ... مختلف أو غير. مختلفين.
rows.why: فرق is the noun 'difference', not 'different'; Amal said 'What is difference? They are different' and he said مختلفين (sheet: different (from) | mu5talef | مختلف). He first used farq at 59:14.

rows.medi_said: your friends which are masculine, so هداك. ... Right? هداك?
rows.amal_said: شو؟ ... غير عن. What does this mean?
rows.why: 'these' (plural) is هدول not the singular far هداك; Amal asked شو؟ / what does it mean and he said هدول.
Plain present needs b- (Amal just said بشوفك); she let it pass, could be the engine.
